title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Provisions on the Application by Securities Regulatory Authorities to the People's Courts for Freezing of Capital Accounts and Securities Accounts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Provisions on Securities Regulatory Authorities Applying to the People's Courts for Freezing of Capital Accounts and Securities Accounts"

Fa [2005] No. 55

To the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Securities Law and other laws and regulations, as well as the needs of actual work, our court has formulated the "Provisions on Securities Regulatory Authorities Applying to the People's Courts for Freezing of Capital Accounts and Securities Accounts," which are hereby issued to you for implementation. At the same time, the following matters are clarified:

I. Internal division of work within the People's Court. Upon receipt of an application from a securities regulatory authority for freezing a capital account or securities account, the People's Court shall register it with the Case Filing Division and promptly transfer it to the Administrative Division for review, which shall render a ruling on whether to accept the case. Where the People's Court rules to freeze a capital account or securities account, the Administrative Division shall execute the ruling.

II. Collection of fees. Where the People's Court accepts a case for an application to freeze a capital account or securities account, a case acceptance fee of not more than RMB 10,000 shall be collected for each case. If continued freezing is necessary after the freezing period expires, no additional acceptance fee shall be collected. The actual expenses incurred for the freezing measures shall be borne by the applicant.

All localities shall carefully study any problems encountered during implementation and promptly report them to our court.

April 29, 2005
